title: Go SDK: streaming drain and context shutdown patterns
creator: Marcus Lee
description: Implement a Go SDK pattern for graceful streaming shutdown and context propagation that balances low-latency client cancellations with server-side drain windows. Deliver a canonical helper in the SDK, examples for customers, and unit/integration tests. The goal is to reduce brief spikes of half-open streams and to make client cancellation semantics explicit and ergonomic.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamSession wrapper with CancelWithGrace(gracePeriod time.Duration) and CloseImmediate() semantics
Context cancellation from callers cancels in-flight read/recv but allows a configurable server drain window prior to hard shutdown
Examples in /examples/go/ show common patterns (short-lived request with tight deadline, long-lived streaming consumer, resumable reader)
Unit tests cover deadline normalization, race between server EOF and client cancel, and buffer draining behavior
Integration test against staging runtime demonstrates no more than 1% increase in short-lived error surface for normal workloads and zero regressions for end-to-end request completion
comments: 2025-02-12 Marcus: Spike to prototype a StreamSession wrapper completed. Implemented local cancel+drain logic and measured impact using the synthetic load runner. Observed client cancel without drain closed NVMe pinned goroutines in 0.02% of runs — need stronger guarantee.

2025-02-14 Avery: Design review notes - prefer explicit grace period API instead of implicit sleepy shutdown to avoid surprising latencies. Add an opt-in debug hook to emit stream lifecycle traces to console for early rollout.

2025-02-16 Marcus: Updated proto for wrapper, added CancelWithGrace(ctx, grace) helper. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/214 (WIP). Benchmarks: median latency unchanged; p99 increased by 4ms with a 50ms grace window under adversarial cancellation load.

2025-02-18 QA: Added integration test plan - simulate server-side delayed EOF, client cancels mid-stream, verify no goroutine leak after 10k iterations. Test failure rate initial: 0.6% flakes; root cause: race between socket close and read unblock. Added small backoff and explicit read-unblock to wrapper.

2025-02-20 Marcus: Opened follow-up to add telemetry labels on cancel reason (user_cancel, deadline, network_error). Leaving task In Progress to finalize docs and rollout notes. Patch ready for internal canary.

Reviewer feedback (2025-02-19, Lina): inline docstrings should call out recommended patterns for function-typing: pass ctx from caller, do not derive background contexts inside wrapper. Also request: add example for server-initiated push followed by client cancel.
2025-02-20 Avery: Security review not required for this change, but audit log extension will be a separate ticket if org needs cancel_reason retention.
implementation_notes: Expose StreamSession type that wraps the raw client stream and manages an internal cancelation goroutine
API surface: CancelWithGrace(ctx context.Context, grace time.Duration) error; CloseImmediate() error; WaitDone(ctx) error
Use a small internal buffered channel to drain any already-received messages for up to grace duration, then force-close the underlying transport
Normalize deadlines: if ctx has deadline sooner than grace window, honor ctx deadline and short-circuit grace
Avoid introducing background goroutines for each stream in high-throughput clients; reuse a pooled worker or attach cancellation handling to existing read loop where possible
tests: unit/stream_session_test.go: covers CancelWithGrace, CloseImmediate, WaitDone semantics
e2e/staging-stream-cancel-smoke: validate metrics and log emission on cancel
